concepts.label: Travel Sample Data Model (airline/route/airport/hotel document types)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the sample dataset's own document-type taxonomy (each document carries a primary-key-as-document-ID, an `id` field, and a `type` field), used across many SDK tutorial pages in this batch. No existing registry concept for this specific sample-data schema.

concepts.label: Travel Sample Collections-aware data model (7.0+, tenant agent scopes with users/bookings collections)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a distinct, later evolution of the same sample dataset that adds multi-tenant Scopes/Collections structure, explicitly gated on Server 7.0+ and stated to not exist by default.

relations.subject: sdk:travel-sample-data-model
relations.evidence: The [tutorial introduction to using the SDK](../hello-world/sample-application.md) uses the _Travel Sample_ data bucket.

relations.subject: sdk:travel-sample-collections
relations.evidence: The new version of the Travel Sample application utilises [Collections](../concept-docs/collections.md), introduced in the 7.0 release of Couchbase Server. The application showcases the use of collections and scopes to represent a multi-tenant approach to organizing user and flight data.

relations.subject: sdk:travel-sample-collections
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted-leaning - describes the join query technique required to use this data model, not a strict ordering dependency; kept as the closest fit rather than a weaker seeAlso, since the page frames JOIN/UNNEST as necessary to make sense of the model's foreign-key fields
relations.evidence: SQL++ provides the JOIN feature, something previously not possible in a document database. To join two documents in a SELECT statement, one of them must contain a field whose value is equal to the key of the other document.

relations.subject: sdk:travel-sample-data-model
relations.evidence: Refer to the [Querying with SQL++](../concept-docs/n1ql-query.md) section for more information about using SQL++ with the SDKs.

notable_absence.finding: The Collections-aware variant of the data model is gated on 'Couchbase Server 7.0 or later' in prose, but the page never links this to a version:server-7-0-style registry concept the way other pages in this batch do - it names the requirement inline ('To try this out you need Couchbase Server 7.0 or later') without a markdown link to a version-specific concept page, so I recorded the constraint via isVariantOf's own evidence rather than minting a separate availableSince relation on weaker textual grounds.

cross_component_finding: The airlineid foreign-key pattern described here (a field in one document type holding the primary key of another) is the same JOIN ON KEYS mechanism documented generically for SQL++, applied concretely to this specific sample dataset - a good illustration rather than a new fact.
cross_product_finding: The page notes the travel-sample bucket configuration and installation are managed entirely outside the SDK (Server REST API / install-sample-buckets), reinforcing this batch's general pattern that sample-data provisioning is a Server/Capella-side concern the SDK docs merely consume.
